driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

Every figure used is dated at or before 2026-11-04; the 5 November news-log entries (Asia chip selloff, mixed US futures, premarket earnings) were NOT used.
Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched; the last obtainable implied-volatility values (TLT 30-day IV, EUR/USD 1-month ATM IV, RVX) were carried forward again with stale-source notes.

Category 1-12 votes are neutral unless a dated source in the news log gives a clear 1-day read (Rates, Earnings, Macro calendar and Cross-asset are 1D-only; Fed path is horizon-wide); Trend structure follows the computed structure reads; Market structure carries its own mechanical direction.

newsLog.event: Fox News Decision Desk projected Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress in the midterms. US futures dipped sharply overnight on the early counts, then rebounded as political uncertainty cleared; renewables and health insurers rallied while Trump Media and CoreWeave fell premarket.
newsLog.numbers: Per CNBC (8:45 AM ET): Dow futures ~+1,083 pts (+2.1%), S&P 500 futures ~+1.1%, Nasdaq-100 futures ~+0.4% (overnight low 27,615.75, lowest since Jul 30); Fox earlier showed S&P futures +0.35%; TAN +5% premarket; VIX futures 20.90 Tue evening
newsLog.reaction: Divided-government outcome read as removing election risk; futures swung from deep overnight losses to solid gains.

newsLog.event: Treasury yields eased from Tuesday's surge (10Y up more than 6bp to ~4.96%) and the dollar weakened overnight as the midterm result and softer oil cooled risk aversion. Sources differ slightly on the exact 10Y level.
newsLog.reaction: Lower yields and a softer dollar are supportive for bonds and risk assets, though the 10Y remains near 5%.
newsLog.tickers: TLT, 10Y, yield, Treasury, DXY, USD, dollar

newsLog.event: ADP October private payrolls beat estimates. Overnight, gold and silver jumped alongside the weaker dollar, while Japan's Nikkei swung sharply (down 4.45% intraday to its lowest since May) before closing down 1.42%; Kospi rose and the Stoxx 600 opened up.
newsLog.numbers: ADP Oct: +86K vs +75K est (Sep revised to 86K); spot gold +2.93% to $4,043.45; silver +4.44% to $51.98; Nikkei 225 -1.42% to 62,188.63; Kospi +0.62%; ASX 200 -0.59%; Stoxx 600 +0.44% early
newsLog.reaction: Solid private hiring with strong metals bid; Asia mixed with volatile Japan session.

newsLog.event: Markets closed sharply higher and the rally held into the close: Democrats confirmed full control of both the House and Senate (not a split Congress, as some pre-market reports floated). The Dow's post-election-day gain was its best in 44 years.
newsLog.reaction: Removal of election uncertainty plus a 'gridlock is good for stocks' read drove broad buying; small caps and mega-cap tech both rallied hard into the close.

newsLog.event: Apple shares hit an all-time high and market cap topped $5 trillion after a strong fiscal Q4 report, helping lead a mega-cap tech surge. Uber beat Q3 estimates but gave soft Q4 EPS guidance (shares rose anyway); McDonald's beat on EPS despite negative US same-store sales.
newsLog.numbers: Apple fiscal Q4: revenue $114.48B, EPS $2.10, market cap >$5T; ~2:50pm ET moves: Amazon +7.22%, Microsoft +7.07%, Apple +6.27%, Alphabet +4.13%; Uber Q4 EPS guide $0.95-$0.99 vs $1.06 est; McDonald's Q3 EPS $3.57 vs $3.38 est, revenue $7.16B vs $7.28B est, US comp sales -0.2%
newsLog.reaction: AAPL +6.27% to a record high, UBER +3.47%, MCD +4.73%; big tech led index gains alongside the post-election relief rally.
newsLog.tickers: AAPL, AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL, UBER, MCD
newsLog.vsExp: Apple beat; Uber Q3 beat / Q4 guide miss; McDonald's EPS beat / revenue miss
